goal: decision-models S5 (application point A4; BR-DEC-4, BR-DEC-6). A maintainer can measure offline whether a decision model tells a new blocking Review finding apart as the same invariant class as an earlier one, a new defect, or out of contract, and how many rounds that would save. Delegated choices: point a4_finding_equivalence (input_category finding, sensitive; options same_invariant, new_defect, out_of_contract); scripts/decision-eval/a4/extract.ts emits one row per review finding at round >= 2 of committed runs with >= 5 review rework rounds, with earlier findings as context, keeping gold labels on re-extraction; run.ts uses the eval harness with baseline same_acceptance and reports per task first_correct_grouping_round beside repeat_trigger_round from acceptanceRepeatSeries. Finding text leaves the machine only when egress enables finding.

acceptance.assertion: In tests/decision-eval-a4.test.ts, extract.ts on a temporary git repository committing one run with 6 review rework rounds and one run with 2 emits rows only for the 6-round run, only for findings at round >= 2, each carrying its earlier findings; re-extraction keeps a gold label set on an existing row; an invalid gold label exits 1 naming the row.

In tests/decision-eval-a4.test.ts, run.ts with a provider whose egress does not list finding records every case unavailable with egress_denied and makes zero fetch calls; with egress listing finding and the fake provider it writes a report containing the same_acceptance baseline, per-option metrics, calibration and, per task, first_correct_grouping_round and repeat_trigger_round.
